LESSON: READING 12.4.1: SHORT STORY: CHARACTERS (CLASS READER)

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 12
Topic 12.4: Reading 12.4.1: Short Story: Characters (Class Reader)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 12.4.1: Short Story: Characters (Class Reader), part of Strand 12 in Grade 8 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: What qualities do you admire in people? 2. How can character traits be described?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. read a story in print or non-print form,

2. identify the characters in the story as they have read,

3. categorize the characters as good or bad based on their actions and words, with peers,

4. read a short story and discuss the actions and words of the characters in the story,

5. write paragraphs describing the traits of the characters in the short story using different words and expressions,

6. work with peers to compare and contrast the traits of the characters in the short story,

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. read a story in print or non-print form,
2. identify the characters in the story as they have read,
3. categorize the characters as good or bad based on their actions and words, with peers,
4. read a short story and discuss the actions and words of the characters in the story,
5. write paragraphs describing the traits of the characters in the short story using different words and expressions,
6. work with peers to compare and contrast the traits of the characters in the short story,

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 12.4.1: Short Story: Characters (Class Reader) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Critical thinking: It is developed as the learner analyses characters in the short story.

• Problem solving: It is developed as the learner relates characters in the story to those in real life.

Values:
Unity: It is promoted as the learner displays team spirit while role playing the different characters in the short story.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Peace education: It is promoted as the learner appreciates the fact that different people have different traits.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Characterisation is a relevant concept in learning of literary skills in Kiswahili and Religious Education
